title: Evolvable competency decouples genotypic from phenotypic fitness

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolvable competency decouples genotypic from phenotypic fitness

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model with evolvable competency, the correlation between genotypic and phenotypic fitness fell to zero within about 20 generations, so allowing competency to evolve disrupts selection's ability to pick the best structural genes.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.4. Evolution Results in a High, Constant Level of Competency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Correlation dropped to 0 within about 20 generations as individuals who succeeded because of their developmental competencies rapidly dominated the population. We conclude that allowing competency to evolve disrupts the ability to select for the best structural genes.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “3. Results › 3.4. Evolution Results in a High, Constant Level of Competency”. Scope: In silico 1D artificial embryos with an evolvable competency gene

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-08: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.89

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both fitness variables and the temporal criterion are explicit outputs of a simple model. The claim is straightforward to replicate and stress-test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: At each generation compute the population correlation between pre-development and post-development fitness in replicated evolvable-competency runs. Persistence of a substantial correlation beyond about 20 generations would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Correlation near zero can depend on ceiling effects in phenotypic fitness.

The causal wording is specific to this selection scheme.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both fitnesses are defined in the model and emitted by the evolvable-competency experiment. A correlation trajectory is a standard calculation on those outputs. If the correlation stays high, the claim that evolving competency blocks selection on structural genes in this model is refuted.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the evolvable-competency runs, compute the correlation of genotypic and phenotypic fitness each generation. A fall to about zero by generation 20, while phenotypic fitness stays high, would confirm the claim; a correlation that remains strongly positive would refute decoupling.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: The generation at which correlation hits zero is seed-sensitive and should be summarized over repeats.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In a re-implementation of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) evolvable-competency model, the correlation between genotypic and phenotypic fitness across the individuals of a population falls from high values to about zero within about 20 generations and stays there.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered design: 30 repeats x 1000 generations (the evolvable-competency simulator of levin-2023-competency-07 with independent seeds). Primary statistic, as the claim states it ('for all individuals in these populations'): each generation, the Pearson correlation across the 100 individuals between genotypic and phenotypic fitness (undefined when phenotypic fitness is constant; such generations are excluded and counted), averaged over repeats. Pass if all of: mean r at generation 1 >= 0.5; mean r over generations 21-40 <= 0.1; mean r over generations 41-1000 <= 0.1.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: refutes if the mean r over generations 21-40 or over generations 41-1000 is >= 0.3. Anything else not meeting the pass criterion -> mixed. Reported but not entering the verdict: the authors' code statistic (Pearson correlation between the repeat-mean best genotypic and best phenotypic fitness curves within 10-generation bins, NaN set to 0) and the selection differential on genotypic fitness (mean genotypic fitness of the 10 selected parents minus the population mean).
